source: Consumer Policy Center report via Inman, Nov. 17, 2026

headline: Illinois sets the bar
on *agent records*
slides.fig_caption: Illinois' score in a 50-state review of how license lookups show agent discipline. The top mark.
slides.sub: Only 2 of the 47 states rated earned a "good" grade: Illinois and Arizona.

slides.title: How *47 states* graded
slides.note: Scored on findability, plain-language explanation and work history. *16 states scored zero.* Kentucky, Washington and Wyoming couldn't be rated.

slides.label: states flag discipline in the *first result* a consumer sees
slides.body: Illinois, Delaware and Idaho. Only Illinois also explains the action in plain language. It lost a point for not listing past brokerages.

slides.label: of 47 states where an AI search *found no record*
slides.body: Given an agent's name, license number and state, the AI came up empty, which a consumer could mistake for a clean record.

slides.title: Know your *own record*
slides.body: The report urges states to flag actions in search results, list past brokerages and keep records public longer. These are recommendations, not rules. Check your own license page so you know what clients see.
